pairs.fullEnglish: Jacob sent messengers ahead of him to his brother Esau, to the land of שֵׂעִיר, to the territory of Edom.
He instructed them, saying, ‘This is what you shall say to my master, to Esau: Thus says your servant Jacob: I have lived with Laban and have remained until now.
I have acquired cattle and donkeys, sheep, male servants and female servants. I have sent to inform my master, to find favor in your eyes.’
The messengers returned to Jacob, saying, ‘We came to your brother, to Esau, and he too is coming to meet you, with four hundred men with him.’
Jacob was very afraid and was distressed. He divided the people who were with him, and the sheep, the cattle and the camels, into two camps.
He said, ‘If Esau comes to one camp and strikes it, the camp that remains will be able to escape.’
Jacob said, ‘God of my father Abraham and God of my father Isaac, יְיָ, who said to me, “Return to your land and to your birthplace, and I will do good to you”:
My merits are small in comparison with all the acts of kindness and all the benefits that You have done for Your servant, for I crossed this Jordan alone, and now I have become two camps.
Rescue me now from the hand of my brother, from the hand of Esau, for I am afraid of him, lest he come and strike me down, mother together with children.
Yet You said, “I will surely do good to you, and I will make your children as numerous as the sand of the sea, which cannot be counted because of its abundance.”’
He spent that night there and took, from what he had brought in his possession, a gift for his brother Esau:
Two hundred female goats and twenty male goats, two hundred ewes and twenty rams;
Thirty nursing camels with their young, forty cows and ten bulls, twenty female donkeys and ten young male donkeys.
He put them in the hands of his servants, each herd separately, and said to his servants, ‘Pass on ahead of me, and leave a space between one herd and the next.’
He instructed the first, saying, ‘When my brother Esau meets you and questions you, saying, “To whom do you belong, where are you going, and whose are these ahead of you?”’
‘You shall say, “They belong to your servant, to Jacob. It is a gift being sent to my master, to Esau; and look, he too is coming behind us.”’
He also instructed the second, the third, and all those going behind the herds, saying, ‘Speak to Esau in these terms when you find him.

You shall also say, “Look, your servant Jacob is coming behind us.”’ For he said, ‘I will quiet his anger with the gift going ahead of me, and afterward I will see his face; perhaps he will show me favor.’
The gift passed on ahead of him, while he spent that night in the camp.
He rose that night and took his two wives, his two concubines and his eleven sons, and crossed the ford of יוּבְקָא.
He took them and brought them across the stream, and brought across what belonged to him.
Jacob was left alone, and a man wrestled with him until dawn rose.
He saw that he could not overcome him, and touched the broad part of his thigh. The broad part of Jacob’s thigh was dislocated as he wrestled with him.
He said, ‘Let me go, for dawn has risen.’ He said, ‘I will not let you go unless you bless me.’
He said to him, ‘What is your name?’ He said, ‘Jacob.’
He said, ‘Your name shall no longer be called Jacob, but Israel, for you have become great before יְיָ and with men, and you have prevailed.’
Jacob asked and said, ‘Tell me your name now.’ He said, ‘Why is it that you ask my name?’ And he blessed him there.
Jacob called the name of the place פְּנִיאֵל, ‘For I have seen the angels of יְיָ face to face, and my life has been saved.’
The sun rose for him as he passed פְּנוּאֵל, and he was limping on his thigh.
Therefore the children of Israel do not eat the sinew of the hip that is on the broad part of the thigh, to this day, because he touched the broad part of Jacob’s thigh, at the sinew of the hip.
Jacob raised his eyes and saw, and there was Esau coming, with four hundred men with him. He divided the children among Leah, Rachel and the two concubines.
He placed the concubines and their children first, Leah and her children behind them, and Rachel and Joseph last.
He himself passed ahead of them and bowed to the ground seven times, until he drew near to his brother.
Esau ran to meet him, embraced him, fell upon his neck and kissed him, and they wept.
He raised his eyes and saw the women and the children, and said, ‘Who are these to you?’ He said, ‘The children with whom יְיָ has favored your servant in compassion.’
The concubines approached, they and their children, and bowed.
Leah too approached with her children, and they bowed; afterward Joseph and Rachel approached and bowed.
He said, ‘What do you mean by all this camp that I encountered?’ He said, ‘To find favor in my master’s eyes.’
Esau said, ‘I have much, my brother; prosper with what is yours.’
Jacob said, ‘Please, if I have now found favor in your eyes, accept my gift from my hand, for I have seen your face as one sees the face of great men, and you have received me favorably.
He said, ‘Let us set out and go, and I will go alongside you.’
He said to him, ‘My master knows that the children are tender, and the nursing sheep and cattle are my responsibility. If they are driven hard for one day, all the sheep will die.
Let my master now pass ahead of his servant, and I will lead on gently, at the pace of the livestock ahead of me and at the pace of the children, until I come to my master in שֵׂעִיר.’
Esau said, ‘Let me now leave with you some of the people who are with me.’ He said, ‘Why this? Let me find favor in my master’s eyes.’
On that day Esau returned on his way to שֵׂעִיר.
Jacob journeyed to סֻכּוֹת and built himself a house, and made shelters for his livestock. Therefore he called the name of the place סֻכּוֹת.
Jacob came safely to the city of שְׁכֶם, which is in the land of Canaan, on his return from פַּדַּן דַּאֲרָם, and camped opposite the city.
He bought the holding in the field where he had pitched his tent from the sons of חֲמוֹר, the father of שְׁכֶם, for one hundred lambs.
He erected an altar there and worshiped upon it before אֵל, the God of Israel.
Dinah, the daughter of Leah whom she had borne to Jacob, went out to see the daughters of the land.
שְׁכֶם, son of חֲמוֹר the Hivite, the ruler of the land, saw her. He took her, lay with her and violated her.
His soul was drawn to Dinah, Jacob’s daughter. He loved the young woman and spoke to the young woman’s heart.
שְׁכֶם said to his father חֲמוֹר, ‘Take this young woman for me as a wife.’
Jacob heard that he had defiled his daughter Dinah. His sons were with his livestock in the field, and Jacob remained silent until they came.
חֲמוֹר, the father of שְׁכֶם, went out to Jacob to speak with him.

Jacob’s sons came in from the field when they heard. The men were grieved and greatly angered, because he had committed a disgraceful act in Israel by lying with Jacob’s daughter, and such a thing was not fit to be done.
חֲמוֹר spoke with them, saying, ‘My son שְׁכֶם’s soul is drawn to your daughter. Give her to him now as a wife.
Intermarry with us: give your daughters to us, and take our daughters for yourselves.
You shall live with us, and the land shall be before you. Settle, conduct trade in it, and acquire holdings in it.’
שְׁכֶם said to her father and her brothers, ‘Let me find favor in your eyes, and whatever you say to me I will give.
Set the bride-price and gifts very high upon me, and I will give as you tell me; only give me the young woman as a wife.’
Jacob’s sons answered שְׁכֶם and his father חֲמוֹר with shrewdness, and spoke because he had defiled their sister Dinah.
They said to them, ‘We cannot do this thing, to give our sister to a man who has a foreskin, for that is a disgrace to us.
Only on this condition will we agree to you: if you become like us, by circumcising every male among you.
Then we will give our daughters to you and take your daughters for ourselves; we will live with you and become one people.
But if you will not accept our demand to be circumcised, we will take our daughter and go.’
Their words were pleasing in the eyes of חֲמוֹר and in the eyes of שְׁכֶם, son of חֲמוֹר.
The young man did not delay in doing the thing, for he desired Jacob’s daughter, and he was more honored than all his father’s household.
חֲמוֹר and his son שְׁכֶם came to the gate of their city and spoke with the men of their city, saying:

‘These men are at peace with us. Let them settle in the land and conduct trade in it; look, the land is wide open before them. Let us take their daughters for ourselves as wives and give our daughters to them.
Only on this condition will the men agree to us, to live with us and become one people: that every male among us be circumcised, as they are circumcised.
Their livestock, their property and all their beasts—will they not be ours? Only let us agree to them, and they will live with us.’
All who went out through the gate of his city accepted the words of חֲמוֹר and his son שְׁכֶם. Every male was circumcised, all who went out through the gate of his city.

On the third day, when their pains had grown severe upon them, two of Jacob’s sons, Simeon and Levi, Dinah’s brothers, each took his sword. They entered the city whose inhabitants were dwelling securely, and killed every male.
They killed חֲמוֹר and his son שְׁכֶם with the edge of the sword, took Dinah from שְׁכֶם’s house, and went out.
Jacob’s sons came in to strip the slain and plundered the city because they had defiled their sister.
They took captive and plundered all their possessions, all their little ones and their wives, and everything that was in the houses.

Jacob said to Simeon and Levi, ‘You have brought trouble upon me by putting enmity between us and the inhabitants of the land, the Canaanites and the Perizzites. I am a people few in number; they will gather against me and strike me, and I shall be destroyed, I and the people of my household.’
יְיָ said to Jacob, ‘Arise, go up to Bais El and live there, and make an altar there to the God who was revealed to you when you fled from your brother Esau.’
Jacob said to the people of his household and to all who were with him, ‘Remove the idols of the nations that are among you, purify yourselves, and change your clothing.
Let us arise and go up to Bais El, and I will make an altar there to the God who accepted my prayer on the day of my distress, and whose Word was my support on the way that I traveled.’
They gave Jacob all the idols of the nations that were in their hands and the earrings that were in their ears. Jacob hid them beneath the terebinth that was by שְׁכֶם.
They journeyed, and a fear from יְיָ came upon the peoples in the cities around them, and they did not pursue Jacob’s sons.
Jacob came to לוּז, which is in the land of Canaan—that is Bais El—he and all the people who were with him.
He built an altar there and called the place אֵל בֵּית אֵל, for there יְיָ was revealed to him when he fled from his brother.
Deborah, Rebecca’s nurse, died and was buried below Bais El, at the lower edge of the plain, and he called its name ‘The Plain of Weeping.’
יְיָ was revealed to Jacob again when he came from פַּדַּן אֲרָם, and blessed him.
יְיָ said to him, ‘Your name is Jacob. Your name shall no longer be called Jacob, but Israel shall be your name.’ And He called his name Israel.
יְיָ said to him, ‘I am אֵל שַׁדַּי. Be fruitful and multiply; a people and an assembly of tribes shall come from you, and kings who rule over peoples shall come forth from you.
The land that I gave to Abraham and Isaac I will give to you, and to your children after you I will give the land.’
The glory of יְיָ ascended from above him at the place where He had spoken with him.
Jacob erected a pillar at the place where He had spoken with him, a pillar of stone. He poured libations upon it and poured oil upon it.
Jacob called the name of the place where יְיָ had spoken with him Bais El.
While she was having difficulty in her labor, the midwife said to her, ‘Do not be afraid, for this one too is a son for you.’
Rachel died and was buried on the road to אֶפְרָת, which is Bais Lechem.
Jacob erected a pillar over her grave; it is the pillar of Rachel’s grave to this day.
Israel journeyed and pitched his tent beyond the tower of עֵדֶר.
While Israel was dwelling in that land, Reuben went and lay with Bilhah, his father’s concubine, and Israel heard. Jacob’s sons were twelve.
The sons of Leah: Jacob’s firstborn Reuben, Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar and Zebulun.
The sons of Rachel: Joseph and Benjamin.
The sons of Bilhah, Rachel’s female servant: Dan and Naphtali.
The sons of Zilpah, Leah’s female servant: Gad and Asher. These are Jacob’s sons who were born to him in פַּדַּן אֲרָם.
Jacob came to his father Isaac at מַמְרֵא, קִרְיַת אַרְבַּע, which is Hebron, where Abraham and Isaac had lived.
The days of Isaac were one hundred and eighty years.
Isaac expired and died and was gathered to his people, old and full of days; his sons Esau and Jacob buried him.
These are the descendants of Esau, who is Edom.
And בָּשְׂמַת, daughter of Ishmael, sister of נְבָיוֹת.
עָדָה bore אֱלִיפָז to Esau, and בָּשְׂמַת bore רְעוּאֵל.
אָהֳלִיבָמָה bore יְעוּשׁ, יַעְלָם and קֹרַח. These are Esau’s sons who were born to him in the land of Canaan.

Esau took his wives, his sons, his daughters, all the persons of his household, his livestock, all his beasts and all the property he had acquired in the land of Canaan, and went to another land, away from his brother Jacob.
For their property was too abundant for them to live together, and the land of their sojourning could not sustain them because of their livestock.
Esau settled in the mountain country of שֵׂעִיר; Esau is Edom.
These are the descendants of Esau, the father of the Edomites, in the mountain country of שֵׂעִיר.
These are the names of Esau’s sons: אֱלִיפַז, son of עָדָה, Esau’s wife; רְעוּאֵל, son of בָּשְׂמַת, Esau’s wife.
The sons of אֱלִיפָז were תֵּימָן, אוֹמָר, צְפוֹ, גַעְתָּם and קְנַז.
תִמְנַע was a concubine of אֱלִיפַז, Esau’s son, and she bore עֲמָלֵק to אֱלִיפַז. These are the sons of עָדָה, Esau’s wife.
These are the sons of רְעוּאֵל: נַחַת, זֶרַח, שַׁמָּה and מִזָּה. These were the sons of בָשְׂמַת, Esau’s wife.
These are the chiefs among Esau’s sons, the sons of אֱלִיפַז, Esau’s firstborn: Chief תֵימָן, Chief אוֹמָר, Chief צְפוֹ, Chief קְנַז;
Chief קֹרַח, Chief גַעְתָּם, Chief עֲמָלֵק. These are the chiefs of אֱלִיפַז in the land of Edom; these are the sons of עָדָה.
These are the sons of רְעוּאֵל, Esau’s son: Chief נַחַת, Chief זֶרַח, Chief שַׁמָּה, Chief מִזָּה. These are the chiefs of רְעוּאֵל in the land of Edom; these are the sons of בָשְׂמַת, Esau’s wife.
These are the sons of אָהֳלִיבָמָה, Esau’s wife: Chief יְעוּשׁ, Chief יַעְלָם, Chief קֹרַח. These are the chiefs of אָהֳלִיבָמָה, daughter of עֲנָה, Esau’s wife.
These are Esau’s sons, and these are their chiefs; he is Edom.
These are the sons of שֵׂעִיר the Horite, the inhabitants of the land: לוֹטָן, שׁוֹבָל, צִבְעוֹן and עֲנָה;
דִשׁוֹן, אֵצֶר and דִישָׁן. These are the chiefs of the Horites, the sons of שֵׂעִיר, in the land of Edom.
The sons of לוֹטָן were חוֹרִי and הֵימָם; לוֹטָן’s sister was תִּמְנָע.
These are the sons of שׁוֹבָל: עַלְוָן, מָנַחַת, עֵיבָל, שְׁפוֹ and אוֹנָם.
These are the sons of צִבְעוֹן: אַיָּה and עֲנָה. This is עֲנָה who found the mighty men in the wilderness while he was tending the donkeys of his father צִבְעוֹן.
These are the children of עֲנָה: דִּשֹׁן and אָהֳלִיבָמָה, daughter of עֲנָה.
These are the sons of דִישָׁן: חֶמְדָּן, אֶשְׁבָּן, יִתְרָן and כְּרָן.
These are the sons of אֵצֶר: בִּלְהָן, זַעֲוָן and עֲקָן.
These are the sons of דִישָׁן: עוּץ and אֲרָן.
These are the chiefs of the Horites: Chief לוֹטָן, Chief שׁוֹבָל, Chief צִבְעוֹן, Chief עֲנָה;
Chief דִשֹׁן, Chief אֵצֶר, Chief דִישָׁן. These are the chiefs of the Horites according to their chieftainships in the land of שֵׂעִיר.
These are the kings who reigned in the land of Edom before a king reigned over the children of Israel.
בֶּלַע, son of בְּעוֹר, reigned in Edom, and the name of his city was דִּנְהָבָה.
בָּלַע died, and יוֹבָב, son of זֶרַח, from בָּצְרָה, reigned in his place.
יוֹבָב died, and חֻשָׁם, from the land of the south, reigned in his place.
חֻשָׁם died, and הֲדַד, son of בְּדַד, who killed the Midianites in the territory of Moab, reigned in his place. The name of his city was עֲוִית.
הֲדָד died, and שַׂמְלָה, from מַּשְׂרֵקָה, reigned in his place.
שַׂמְלָה died, and שָׁאוּל, from רְחוֹבֵי on the Euphrates, reigned in his place.
שָׁאוּל died, and בַּעַל חָנָן, son of עַכְבּוֹר, reigned in his place.
These are the names of Esau’s chiefs, according to their families, their places and their names: Chief תִמְנָע, Chief עַלְוָה, Chief יְתֵת;
Chief אָהֳלִיבָמָה, Chief אֵלָה, Chief פִינֹן;
Chief קְנַז, Chief תֵימָן, Chief מִבְצָר;
Chief מַגְדִּיאֵל, Chief עִירָם. These are the chiefs of Edom according to their settlements in the land of their possession; he is Esau, the father of the Edomites.
They said, ‘Should our sister be treated like a prostitute?’

qualifications.he: הקריאה הראשית יִתְעֲבֵד מנוסחת בסביל: האם ייעשה כך לאחותנו, כאל זונה. החלופה יַעְבֵּד יָת מנוסחת בפעיל: האם הוא ינהג באחותנו כאל זונה. הגוף משקף את הקריאה הראשית ואינו מוחק את החלופה או מוסיף לה שם נושא שאינו כתוב בה.
qualifications.en: The main reading יִתְעֲבֵד is passive: 'Should our sister be treated like a prostitute?' The alternative יַעְבֵּד יָת is active: 'Should he treat our sister like a prostitute?' The body follows the main reading without removing the alternative or inserting a subject's name that the alternative does not state.

pairs.fullEnglish: As her soul departed, for she died, she called his name בַּר דְּוָי (‘Son of Sorrow’); but his father called him Benjamin.

qualifications.he: הגוף מתרגם את הקריאה הראשית מִיתַת: מתה. הקריאה החלופית מַיְתָא מוסרת שהייתה גוססת או עומדת למות. שתיהן מובאות בהקשר יציאת נפשה; אין כאן הכרעה בין צורות הזמן. השם בַּר דְּוָי נמסר כבן הצער, בלי להוסיף כינוי שייכות של גוף ראשון שאינו כתוב בתרגום.
qualifications.en: The body follows the main reading מִיתַת, 'she died'. The alternative מַיְתָא gives 'she was dying'. Both occur in the setting of her soul's departure; the tense alternative is not adjudicated away. בַּר דְּוָי is rendered 'Son of Sorrow', without adding a first-person possessive absent from this Aramaic.

pairs.fullEnglish: Esau took his wives from the daughters of Canaan: עָדָה, daughter of אֵילוֹן the Hittite, and אָהֳלִיבָמָה, daughter of עֲנָה, daughter of צִבְעוֹן the Hivite;

qualifications.he: המקור מוסר רצף יוחסין כפול בלשון בת: אָהֳלִיבָמָה בַּת עֲנָה בַּת צִבְעוֹן. הניסוח האנגלי שומר עליו ואינו מכריע אם בת השנייה מציינת קשר דורי נוסף או כיצד יש לפסק את הרצף. אין להסיק ממנו שעֲנָה נקבה, להחליף בת בבר או ליישב את היוחסין על פי נוסח אחר.
qualifications.en: The source gives the successive lineage formulas אָהֳלִיבָמָה בַּת עֲנָה בַּת צִבְעוֹן, both using 'daughter'. The English retains that formulation without adjudicating the generational extension of the second 'daughter' or the punctuation of the chain. It does not establish that עֲנָה is female, replace 'daughter' with 'son', or harmonize the lineage to another text.

pairs.fullEnglish: These were the sons of אָהֳלִיבָמָה, daughter of עֲנָה, daughter of צִבְעוֹן, Esau’s wife: she bore יְעוּשׁ, יַעְלָם and קֹרַח to Esau.

qualifications.he: רצף היוחסין בַת עֲנָה בַּת צִבְעוֹן נשמר כלשונו. בתרגום האנגלי אין הכרעה בדבר הזיקה המדויקת של בת השנייה או קיצור דורות אפשרי. אין לקרוא בו קביעה שעֲנָה נקבה, ואין לתקן את בת לבר או ליישב את הרצף לפי מקור אחר.
qualifications.en: The lineage sequence בַת עֲנָה בַּת צִבְעוֹן is retained as written. The English does not adjudicate the exact attachment of the second 'daughter' or a possible generational extension. It must not be read as establishing that עֲנָה is female, changing 'daughter' to 'son', or harmonizing the chain to another source.

pairs.fullEnglish: בַּעַל חָנָן, son of עַכְבּוֹר, died, and הֲדַר reigned in his place. The name of his city was פָּעוּ, and the name of his wife was מְהֵיטַבְאֵל, daughter of מַטְרֵד, daughter of a refiner of gold.

qualifications.he: המקור מוסר את ייחוס מְהֵיטַבְאֵל בשני צירופי בת עוקבים, ולאחר השני בא מְצָרֵף דַּהֲבָא, מצרף זהב. האנגלית שומרת את הרצף בלי לקבוע מעבר לכתוב כיצד מתחלקים הדורות או מה מינו של מַטְרֵד. אין להחליף את תיאור מצרף הזהב בשם פרטי ממקור אחר.
qualifications.en: The source gives מְהֵיטַבְאֵל's lineage in two successive 'daughter' formulas, the second followed by מְצָרֵף דַּהֲבָא, 'a refiner of gold'. The English preserves that sequence without settling beyond the wording how the generations are distributed or the sex of מַטְרֵד. The gold-refiner description must not be replaced with a proper name from another text.

pairs.fullEnglish: They plundered their flocks, their cattle and their donkeys, what was in the city and what was in the field.

qualifications.he: הגוף מתרגם את הקריאה הראשית בְּזוֹ: בזזו. הקריאה החלופית שבסוגריים, דְבָרוּ, מוסרת שלקחו או הובילו עמם את הבהמות ואת הנזכר בעיר ובשדה. שתי הקריאות נשמרות; אין כאן הכרעה ביניהן.
qualifications.en: The body follows the main reading בְּזוֹ, 'plundered'. The parenthesized alternative דְבָרוּ says that they took or carried off the animals and the things mentioned in the city and field. Both readings are retained; neither is adjudicated away.

pairs.fullEnglish: Behold, I have made you weak among the nations; you are greatly despised.
The wickedness of your heart has misled you, for you are like an eagle that dwells among the crags of a rock, whose dwelling is on high, saying in its heart: Who will bring me down to the ground?
If you rise high like an eagle, and if you place your dwelling among the stars, from there I will bring you down, says יְיָ.
How Esau has been searched out! His hidden stores have been uncovered.
He was passing through the street opposite her corner, walking along the road to her house.
She seized him and kissed him; she made her face brazen and said to him:

All the men of your covenant have exiled you from your territory; the men at peace with you have misled you and prevailed against you. Those who eat at your table have placed a stumbling block beneath you, because there is no understanding in you.
Will I not, at that time, says יְיָ, destroy the wise from Edom and every man who has understanding from Esau's fortified city?
Because you plundered your brother Jacob, shame will cover you, and you will be wiped out forever.
Sacrificial offerings were incumbent upon me; today I have fulfilled my vows.
I have sprinkled my bed with myrrh, saffron, and cinnamon.
On the day you stood opposite, on the day the nations plundered his possessions and foreigners entered his towns and cast lots over Jerusalem, you too were like one of them.
For near is the day destined to come from before יְיָ upon all the nations. As you have done, so it will be done to you; your recompense will return upon your head.
Come, let us delight in love until morning, and let us occupy ourselves with one another in desire.
For the husband is not at home; he has gone on a distant journey.
He took a bundle of silver in his hand, and on the day of the festival he will come home.

Those of the house of Jacob will be strong like fire, and those of the house of Joseph mighty like a flame, while those of the house of Esau will be weak like straw. They will rule over them and kill them, and there will be no survivor for the house of Esau, for יְיָ has so decreed.

The inhabitants of the south will take possession of Esau's fortified city, and the inhabitants of the lowland will take possession of the land of the Philistines. They will take possession of the towns of Ephraim and the towns of Samaria, and those of the house of Benjamin will take possession of the inhabitants of the land of Gilead.

The exiles of this people of the children of Israel who are in the land of the Canaanites as far as Zarephath, and the exiles of Jerusalem who are in אַסְפַּמְיָא, will take possession of the towns of the southern land.
Deliverers will ascend Mount Zion to judge Esau's fortified city, and the kingship of ייָ will be revealed over all the inhabitants of the earth.
And now, children, listen to me, and give heed to the utterance of my mouth.
Let your heart not turn aside to her ways, and do not stray into her paths.
Her house is the ways to the underworld, descending to the chambers of the grave.
For this reason wisdom calls out, and understanding raises her voice.
A word of prophecy from before יְיָ came to Jonah son of Amittai, saying:
Arise, go to Nineveh, the great city, and prophesy against it, for their wickedness has risen before Me.
יָי raised a great wind over the sea, and there was a great storm at sea, and the ship was about to break apart.
At the top of the heights beside the road she is present, and among the paths she stands.
To you, men, I call, and my voice is directed to human beings.
Understand prudence, you simple ones, and let fools gain understanding in their hearts.
Listen, for I speak truth, and the utterance of my mouth is uprightness.
The prophecy of Obadiah. Thus said יְיָ God concerning Edom: We have heard tidings from before יְיָ, and an envoy has been sent among the nations: Arise, and let us make ready against her for battle.
She is rebellious and restless; her feet do not stay at home.

qualifications.he: התיאור חסרת מנוחה משקף כאן את פָרִדְתָּא בצמוד לאמירה שרגליה אינן שוכנות בבית. אין בו קביעה של מעשה נפרד או של משמעות טכנית לתואר.
qualifications.en: Restless renders פָרִדְתָּא in connection with the statement that her feet do not stay at home. It does not posit a separate deed or a technical meaning for the adjective.

pairs.fullEnglish: And because you looked on at your brother's day, on the day of his downfall; and because you rejoiced over the children of Judah on the day of their downfall; and because you spoke so many boastful things at a time of distress.
He led him astray with the abundance of her words, and with the smoothness of her lips she enticed him.

qualifications.he: הפועל הראשון וְאַטְעֵי נמסר בצורת זכר, ולכן תורגם הוא הטעה אותו, בלי לזהות את הנושא בשם. הכינויים הנשיים בדבריה ובשפתיה, וכן פעולת הפיתוי הנשית שבהמשך, נשמרים בנפרד; צורת המקור אינה מתוקנת לנקבה.
qualifications.en: The opening וְאַטְעֵי is supplied in a masculine form and is rendered he led him astray without naming its subject. The feminine possessives in her words and her lips, and the woman's enticement in the following clause, are retained separately; the source form is not corrected to feminine.

pairs.fullEnglish: For she has brought down many slain, and all those slain are mighty men.
If thieves came upon you, if plunderers by night, how were you sleeping until they had stolen their fill? And if robbers came upon you like grape-gatherers, would they not leave gleanings?
At one time in the markets, at another in the lanes, she lies in wait opposite every appealing corner.

And because you entered the gates of My people on the day of their downfall; and because you too looked on at his misfortune on the day of his downfall; and because you stretched out your hand against his possessions on the day of his downfall.
And he goes after her calmly, like an ox going to the slaughterer, and like a dog going to a fetter.

The sailors were afraid, and each man prayed to his object of worship; they saw that there was no help in them. They threw the articles that were in the ship into the sea to lighten the burden upon themselves. But Jonah had gone down to the bottom of an interior compartment of the ship, and lay down and slept.

qualifications.he: הצירוף מתאר ירידה לתחתית חלל פנימי באונייה. התרגום אינו קובע שהחלל שימש לאחסון, שהיה חדר פרטי או שהייתה לו צורת בנייה מסוימת.
qualifications.en: The phrase describes descent to the bottom of an interior compartment of the ship. The rendering does not specify storage use, a private cabin, or a particular form of construction.

pairs.fullEnglish: And behold, a woman came to meet him, in the attire of a prostitute, one who unsettles the hearts of young men.

qualifications.he: המילה מַפְרְדָא מתארת כאן את פעולתה המפריעה ללב הצעירים. התרגום מערערת שומר על התיאור הרחב, בלי לקבוע אם ההפרעה היא פיזור הדעת, הפרדה או דרך מסוימת של פיתוי.
qualifications.en: מַפְרְדָא describes her disruptive effect on the hearts of young men. Unsettles preserves that broad description without specifying distraction, separation, or a particular means of seduction.

pairs.fullEnglish: I have spread my bed with bedcoverings and with an Egyptian covering.

qualifications.he: הצירוף מוסר תיאור של כיסוי מצרי למיטה. התרגום שומר על משמעות הכיסוי ועל התיאור מצרי, בלי לקבוע סוג בד, אופן אריגה או ניתוח צורני מפורט של קְרִמְתָּא.
qualifications.en: The phrase describes an Egyptian covering for the bed. The rendering retains the covering and its Egyptian description without specifying a fabric, a weaving method, or a detailed morphological analysis of קְרִמְתָּא.

pairs.fullEnglish: And because you stood at the crossroads to wipe out his fugitives; and because you handed over his survivors at a time of distress.
But on Mount Zion there will be deliverance, and they will be holy; those of the house of Jacob will take possession of the property of the nations that had been taking possession of them.

qualifications.he: הסיום שומר את לְהוֹן ככינוי רבים: אותם. בני בית יעקב יירשו את נכסי העמים שהיו מחזיקים בהם; הכינוי אינו מפורש כאן בשם, ואין התרגום קובע פירוט נוסף של ההחזקה הקודמת.
qualifications.en: The ending retains לְהוֹן as the plural pronoun them. Jacob's household will possess the property of the nations that had been taking possession of them; the rendering does not replace the pronoun with a named referent or further specify the earlier possession.

pairs.fullEnglish: For just as you rejoiced over the blow struck against My holy mountain, all the nations will drink the cup of their punishment continually; they will drink and become bewildered, and they will be as though they had never been.

qualifications.he: וְיִסְתַּלְעֲמוּן נמסר כאן ככניסה למצב של מבוכה וטרוף הדעת לאחר השתייה, לא כהיבלעות הגופים ולא כבליעת המשקה בפועל נוסף. רש״י מצטט במפורש 'כְּתַרְגּוּמוֹ: וְיִסְתַּלְעֲמוּן' ומפרש 'לְשׁוֹן מְהוּמָה וְשִׁמָּמוֹן וְטֵרוּף דַּעַת'. זהו הסבר ישיר ללשון התרגום. העמים הם השותים והנבוכים; 'ויהיו כמי שלא היו' נשמר כתוצאה נפרדת ולא כפירוש מילוני לפועל.
qualifications.en: וְיִסְתַּלְעֲמוּן is rendered as becoming bewildered or mentally confounded after drinking, not as their bodies being swallowed or as a further act of gulping the drink. Rashi expressly quotes 'כְּתַרְגּוּמוֹ: וְיִסְתַּלְעֲמוּן' and explains 'לְשׁוֹן מְהוּמָה וְשִׁמָּמוֹן וְטֵרוּף דַּעַת'. This is direct explanation of the Targum's wording. The nations are both the drinkers and those becoming bewildered; their being as though they had never existed remains a separate result, not the verb's lexical definition.

pairs.fullEnglish: And like a stag into whose liver someone sends an arrow flying, he hurries like a bird toward a snare, not knowing that he is going to his own death.

qualifications.he: מַפְרִיחַ נמסר כפועל פעיל וסיבתי: מישהו משלח חץ אל כבדו של האיל. הפועל אינו נוקב בשם המשלח; ׳מישהו׳ באנגלית מוסר נושא בלתי מפורש, ואינו מוסיף זהות של צייד. כינוי השייכות בכַבְדֵיהּ מתייחס לאיל, ואין כאן קביעה שהאיל עצמו משלח את החץ.
qualifications.en: מַפְרִיחַ is rendered as active and causative: someone sends an arrow flying into the stag's liver. The verb does not name the sender; English 'someone' represents an unexpressed agent without identifying a hunter. The possessive suffix in כַבְדֵיהּ refers to the stag, not an assertion that the stag itself sends the arrow.

pairs.fullEnglish: Your mighty men, inhabitants of the south, will be shattered, so that every man who has vigor will be wiped out from Esau's fortified city by slaughter.

qualifications.he: צוֹרְבָא מוסרת כאן עוז או מרץ: תכונה שיש באיש, בהמשך לאזכור הגיבורים. המילה שייכת ללשון להט וחריפות; אין צורך לצמצמה לכוח גופני מסוים. הצירוף המוכר צורבא מרבנן אינו מופיע כאן, ולכן אין האיש מזוהה כתלמיד חכם. גְבַר הוא איש כללי בצלע זו, ולא אדם נוסף שננקב בשמו.
qualifications.en: צוֹרְבָא is rendered here as vigor or mettle, a quality present in the man, following the mention of mighty men. The word belongs to the range of heat, ardor and keenness; no particular kind of bodily strength is specified. The familiar expression צורבא מרבנן does not occur here, so the man is not identified as a scholar. גְבַר is generic in this clause, not an additional named person.

pairs.fullEnglish: They journeyed from בֵּית אֵל, and a ploughing-distance of land still remained before entering אֶפְרָת. רָחֵל gave birth and had difficulty in her labor.

qualifications.he: כְּרוּבַת היא לשון חרישה, ובצירוף כְּרוּבַת אַרְעָא היא מציינת קטע קרקע או מרחק הנקרא על שם החרישה. כאן הוא המרחק שעדיין נותר עד הכניסה לאפרת. אין בצירוף קביעה שהקרקע הייתה אז חרושה, שהוא אורך תלם יחיד, או שיש לו כאן גודל מספרי מסוים; אין המרה ליחידת מרחק מודרנית.
qualifications.en: כְּרוּבַת is ploughing language; כְּרוּבַת אַרְעָא denotes a stretch of ground or distance named in terms of ploughing. Here it is the distance still remaining before entry into אֶפְרָת. The expression does not establish that the ground was then ploughed, that it was one furrow's length, or that it has a particular numerical size here; no modern distance conversion is supplied.

pairs.fullEnglish: יוֹנָה arose to flee to sea before he prophesied in the name of ייָ. He went down to יָפוֹ and found a ship going to sea; he paid the fare and went down into it to go with them at sea before he prophesied in the name of יָי.

qualifications.he: מִן קֳדָם בצירוף דְ ומשפט פועלי נקרא כאן כלשון זמן, ׳לפני שהתנבא בשם ייָ׳. הקריאה נוגעת לנבואה שביחס אליה מתוארת הבריחה; אין זו קביעה שזו הייתה הנבואה הראשונה בחייו. אותו יחס זמן נשמר בחזרה שבסוף הפסוק, מִן קֳדָם דְאִתְנַבֵּי בִּשְׁמָא דַיָי, עם כתיב השם השונה. אין החלפה של המשפט בבריחה ממקום של נוכחות אלוהית, ואין הוספת שם יעד שאינו כתוב בארמית.
qualifications.en: מִן קֳדָם followed by דְ and a verbal clause is read here temporally, ‘before he prophesied in the name of ייָ’. This concerns the prophecy in relation to which the flight is described; it does not assert that this was the first prophecy of his life. The same temporal relation is retained in the closing repetition, מִן קֳדָם דְאִתְנַבֵּי בִּשְׁמָא דַיָי, with its different Divine-name spelling. The clause is not replaced with flight from a location of Divine presence, and no destination name absent from the Aramaic is added.

pairs.fullEnglish: By the gates, at the city's opening and at the entrance of the gates, she is praised and says:

qualifications.he: מִשְׁתַּבְּחָא נמסרת כאן בסביל, ׳היא משובחת׳, כלשון התיאור המקביל של החכמה בשוק. אחר כך נאמר שהיא מדברת. הצורה יכולה לשמש גם בלשון התפארות עצמית, אך אין הכרח לייחס לחכמה פעולה זו כאן. לשון השבח נשמרת ואינה מוחלפת בפועל של קריאה.
qualifications.en: מִשְׁתַּבְּחָא is rendered passively here, 'she is praised,' as in the parallel description of wisdom in the marketplace. She then speaks. The form can also express self-praise, but that action need not be attributed to wisdom here. The praise language is retained rather than replaced by a verb of calling.

pairs.fullEnglish: ‘Accept now my gift that has been brought to you, for there has been compassion upon me (before) יְיָ, and because I have everything.’ He pressed him, and he accepted.

qualifications.he: קדם נשמר בסוגריים ונמסר באנגלית before. הניסוח נותן כבוד כלפי מעלה ונמנע מהשוואת פעולת האל לפעולת אדם; חלופת הנוסח מוצגת ואינה נמחקת.
qualifications.en: קדם is retained in parentheses and rendered before. The wording preserves reverence toward God rather than assimilating divine action to human action; the textual alternative remains visible.

pairs.fullEnglish: In the evening, as the day was setting, in the darkness of night and in darkness.

qualifications.he: המילה נמסרת כחושך, בלי לייחס הלך רוח ובלי להוסיף עובי או דרגה מסוימת של אפלה.
qualifications.en: The word is rendered darkness, not a mood, without adding thickness or a particular degree of darkness.

pairs.fullEnglish: For this reason I went out to meet you; I was going about in search of an encounter, and I said: I will take you along.

qualifications.he: דמפכא נמסר כהסתובבות לשם מפגש; אחריו באה האמירה ״אוביל אותך״. אין מחליפים את נוסח התרגום בדברי הפסוק העברי על חיפוש ומציאה.
qualifications.en: דמפכא is understood as going about for an encounter, followed by I will take you along. The Targum wording is not replaced by the Hebrew verse’s seeking and finding.

dayTitle.en: Messengers to Esau and the Division of the Camps

explanation.he: יעקב שולח שליחים אל עשו אחיו ומבקש למצוא רחמים בעיניו. כאשר הם מודיעים שעשו בא עם ארבע מאות איש, יעקב חושש ומחלק את האנשים והמקנה לשני מחנות, כדי שהמחנה הנשאר יוכל להינצל אם יותקף האחר.
explanation.en: Jacob sends messengers to his brother Esau and seeks favor in his eyes. When they report that Esau is coming with four hundred men, Jacob fears and divides the people and livestock into two camps, so that the remaining camp can escape if the other is attacked.

dayTitle.en: Jacob’s Prayer for Rescue from His Brother

explanation.he: יעקב פונה אל אלהי אבותיו ומזכיר את הציווי לשוב ואת ההבטחה להיטיב עמו. בנוסח התרגום הוא אומר שזכויותיו קטנות כנגד החסדים והטובות שקיבל, ומבקש הצלה מעשו תוך הזכרת ההבטחה לריבוי בניו.
explanation.en: Jacob addresses the God of his fathers and recalls the command to return and the promise to do good to him. In this rendering he says that his merits are small beside the kindnesses and benefits he has received, and asks to be rescued from Esau while recalling the promise that his children will be numerous.

dayTitle.en: Preparing the Gift and Separating the Herds

explanation.he: יעקב לוקח מן הרכוש שהביא עמו מנחה לעשו, והתרגום מפרט את סוגי הבהמות ומספריהן. הוא מוסר כל עדר בנפרד לעבדיו, מצווה להשאיר רווח בין העדרים ומכין את הראשון לשאלות הצפויות מאחיו.
explanation.en: Jacob takes a gift for Esau from the property he has brought with him, and the passage specifies the kinds and numbers of animals. He entrusts each herd separately to his servants, orders spaces between the herds, and prepares the first servant for the questions his brother will ask.

dayTitle.en: Quieting Anger and Bringing the Family across the Stream

explanation.he: יעקב מצווה את הולכי העדרים לחזור על אותו מסר: המנחה נשלחת ממנו, וגם הוא בא אחריהם. התרגום מפרש את כוונתו כהנחת כעסו של עשו, ולאחר שילוח המנחה יעקב מעביר את נשיו, פילגשיו, בניו ורכושו בנחל.
explanation.en: Jacob instructs those accompanying the herds to repeat the same message: the gift is sent by him, and he too is coming behind them. The rendering states his intention as quieting Esau’s anger; after sending the gift ahead, Jacob brings his wives, concubines, sons and possessions across the stream.

dayTitle.he: המאבק עד עלות השחר והשם ישראל
dayTitle.en: The Struggle until Dawn and the Name Israel

explanation.he: יעקב נשאר לבדו ונאבק עם איש עד עלות השחר, ונפגע בירכו במהלך המאבק. הוא אינו מסכים לשלח את האיש בלי ברכה, והלה מכריז על השם ישראל; התרגום מתאר את יעקב כמי שגדל לפני יי ועם אנשים ויכול.
explanation.en: Jacob remains alone and wrestles with a man until dawn, suffering an injury to his thigh during the struggle. He refuses to let the man go without a blessing, and the man announces the name Israel; the rendering describes Jacob as having become great before יְיָ and with men, and as having prevailed.

dayTitle.he: מפניאל אל המפגש עם עשו וההגעה לשכם
dayTitle.en: From פְּנִיאֵל to the Meeting with Esau and Arrival at שְׁכֶם

explanation.he: יעקב מתאר ראיית מלאכי יי פנים בפנים והצלת נפשו, והקטע קושר את הפגיעה בירך לאי אכילת הגיד. לאחר המפגש עם עשו וקבלת המנחה, יעקב מבקש להתקדם בנחת לפי כוח הילדים והמקנה. בהמשך הוא קונה חלקת שדה ועובד על מזבח לפני אל אלהי ישראל; סיום הקריאה מתאר את יציאת דינה ואת הפגיעה בה.
explanation.en: Jacob describes seeing the angels of יְיָ face to face and the saving of his life, and the passage links his thigh injury to not eating the sinew. After meeting Esau and obtaining his acceptance of the gift, Jacob asks to travel gently at the pace of the children and livestock. He later buys a field holding and worships on an altar before אֵל, the God of Israel; the reading ends with Dinah’s departure and the violation of her.

dayTitle.he: משבר שכם, ההתגלות בבית אל ותולדות אדום
dayTitle.en: The Crisis at שְׁכֶם, Revelation at Bais El, and the Descendants of Edom

explanation.he: הקריאה מתארת את הצעת החיתון, התנאי למילה, הריגת אנשי העיר וחששו של יעקב מן האיבה שנוצרה. בבית אל מודגשים קבלת תפילתו של יעקב, סעד המימרא, ההתגלות והסתלקות היקר; בהמשך מסופרים מות רחל ומות יצחק. רשימות התולדות והמושלים של אדום שומרות על קשרי המשפחה, ובתרגום נזכרים גם הגיבורים שמצא ענה ומצרף הזהב שבייחוס אשת הדר.
explanation.en: The reading describes the proposed marriages, the condition of circumcision, the killing of the city’s men, and Jacob’s fear of the resulting enmity. At Bais El it emphasizes the acceptance of Jacob’s prayer, the support of the Word, revelation, and the ascent of the glory; the deaths of Rachel and Isaac follow. The lists of Edom’s descendants and rulers preserve family relationships, and this rendering also mentions the mighty men found by עֲנָה and the gold refiner in the ancestry of הֲדַר’s wife.

dayTitle.en: Edom's confidence in its lofty dwelling is shaken

explanation.he: נבואת עובדיה פותחת בבשורה על היערכות העמים למלחמה באדום. התרגום מתאר את רשע הלב המטעה ואת הדמיון לנשר השוכן במרומי הסלע. גם מגורים בין הכוכבים אינם מונעים את ההורדה, ואוצרות עשו הנסתרים נחשפים.
explanation.en: Obadiah's prophecy opens with tidings of the nations preparing for battle against Edom. The Targum describes the heart's misleading wickedness and compares Edom to an eagle dwelling high among rocky crags. Even a dwelling among the stars cannot prevent its descent, and Esau's hidden stores are exposed.

dayTitle.en: The encounter on the road to temptation

explanation.he: הקטע עוקב אחר ההולך ברחוב ובדרך אל בית האישה עם רדת היום. האישה יוצאת לקראתו בלבוש זונה, ואינה נשארת בביתה אלא אורבת במקומות המעבר. היא תופסת אותו, מנשקת אותו ופונה אליו בעזות פנים.
explanation.en: The passage follows a man walking through the street toward the woman's house as daylight fades. She approaches him dressed as a prostitute and, rather than staying at home, lies in wait in public passageways. She seizes him, kisses him, and addresses him with a brazen face.

dayTitle.he: דברי האישה על נדרים והכנת מיטתה
dayTitle.en: The woman's claims about vows and her prepared bed

explanation.he: האישה אומרת שהשלימה את נדריה ומספרת שיצאה לפגוש את האיש. בהמשך דבריה היא מתארת את כיסויי מיטתה ואת הבשמים שפיזרה עליה. התרגום מונה מור, כורכמא וקינמון, כחלק מדברי הפיתוי שלה.
explanation.en: The woman says that she has fulfilled her vows and tells the man that she went out to meet him. She then describes her bedcoverings and the perfumes she has sprinkled on the bed. The Targum names myrrh, saffron, and cinnamon as part of her enticement.

dayTitle.he: מעשי אדום ביום שברו של אחיו
dayTitle.en: Edom's deeds on the day of its brother's downfall

explanation.he: אדום מתוארת כמי שנעמדה מנגד בעת ביזת נכסי אחיה ונעשתה כאחד התוקפים. הקטע מונה שמחה בשבר, דיבורי גאווה, שליחת יד בנכסים ופגיעה בנמלטים ובניצולים. סופו מודיע כי ביום הבא מלפני יְיָ ישוב הגמול על ראש העושה.
explanation.en: Edom is described as standing opposite while its brother's possessions were plundered and as becoming like one of the attackers. The passage enumerates rejoicing at downfall, boastful speech, seizure of property, and attacks on fugitives and survivors. It closes by announcing that on the day coming from before יְיָ, the doer's recompense will return upon his own head.

dayTitle.en: The promise of a night together and the walk toward a trap

explanation.he: האישה מזמינה את האיש לאהבה עד הבוקר וטוענת שבעלה רחוק ויחזור ביום החג. דבריה המרובים וחלקות שפתיה מטים אותו אחריה. התרגום מדמה את הליכתו לשור ההולך אל השוחט ולכלב ההולך אל הכבל.
explanation.en: The woman invites the man to love until morning and claims that her husband is far away and will return on the festival day. Her many words and smooth lips draw him after her. The Targum compares his going to an ox approaching the slaughterer and a dog approaching a fetter.

dayTitle.he: החכמה מדברת בשערים אל בני האדם
dayTitle.en: Wisdom addresses humanity at the gates

explanation.he: החכמה ניצבת בראשי הגבהים, בדרכים ובפתחי העיר. קולה פונה אל בני האדם וקורא לפתאים להבין ערמה ולכסילים להשכיל בלבם. היא מבקשת שיקשיבו לדבריה, המתוארים כאמת וכיושר.
explanation.en: Wisdom stands on the heights, along the roads, and at the city's entrances. Her voice addresses human beings, calling on the simple to understand prudence and on fools to gain understanding in their hearts. She asks them to listen to speech characterized as truth and uprightness.

dayTitle.en: The warning of death and the contrasting voice of wisdom

explanation.he: הקטע מתאר הליכה אל המוות בלי ידיעה, בדימוי לציפור הממהרת אל הפח. הדובר פונה לילדים ומזהיר שלא לנטות אל דרכי האישה, שביתה מוליך אל שאול ואל חדרי הקבר. בסיום הקריאה נפתח הקול האחר: החכמה קוראת והתבונה מרימה את קולה.
explanation.en: The passage depicts a man unknowingly going toward death, comparing his haste to a bird approaching a snare. The speaker addresses the children and warns them not to turn toward the woman's ways, for her house leads to the underworld and the chambers of the grave. The reading ends with the contrasting voice: wisdom calls and understanding raises her voice.

dayTitle.he: בריתות בוגדות והעונש על ביזת האח
dayTitle.en: Treacherous alliances and punishment for plundering a brother

explanation.he: כל בעלי הברית של אדום מגלים אותה מתחומה; אנשי שלומה מטעים אותה וגוברים עליה, ואוכלי שולחנה מניחים מכשול תחתיה. הנבואה מודיעה על אובדן החכמים מאדום ועל שבירת גיבוריה, יושבי הדרום. הבושה והכיליון נקשרים במפורש לביזת יעקב אחיו.
explanation.en: All Edom's covenant partners exile it from its territory; those at peace with it mislead it and prevail against it, and its table companions place a stumbling block beneath it. The prophecy announces the destruction of the wise from Edom and the shattering of its warriors, inhabitants of the south. Shame and destruction are explicitly linked to the plundering of Jacob, its brother.

dayTitle.en: Jonah's commission and flight to sea

explanation.he: יונה בן אמיתי מקבל דבר נבואה לצאת לנינוה ולהתנבא עליה בגלל רעת יושביה. הוא יורד ליפו, מוצא אונייה היוצאת לים, משלם את שכר ההפלגה ויורד אליה; התיאור קושר את בריחתו להתנבאות בשם יְיָ. בסערה המלחים פונים אל מושאי פולחנם ורואים שאין בהם תועלת, משליכים את כלי האונייה לים, ואילו יונה שוכב וישן למטה.
explanation.en: Jonah son of Amittai receives a prophetic word directing him to Nineveh to prophesy against it because of its inhabitants' wickedness. He goes down to Joppa, finds a ship going to sea, pays the fare, and boards it; the account connects his flight with prophesying in the Divine name. During the storm the sailors appeal to their objects of worship and see that they provide no help, then throw the ship's articles into the sea, while Jonah lies asleep below.

dayTitle.en: Deliverance in Zion and the revelation of Divine kingship

explanation.he: התרגום מציב מול השמחה על מכת הר הקודש את כוס פורענותם של העמים ואת הישועה בציון. בית יעקב ובית יוסף מתוארים כחזקים כאש ולהבה, ואילו בית עשו כחלש כקש. הקטע מפרט את הנחלות והגלויות ומסיים בעליית המושיעים ובגילוי מלכות יְיָ על כל יושבי הארץ.
explanation.en: The Targum sets rejoicing over the blow against the holy mountain against the nations' cup of punishment and the deliverance in Zion. Jacob's and Joseph's households are described as strong as fire and flame, while Esau's household is weak as straw. The passage specifies the possessions and exiled communities and ends with the ascent of deliverers and the revelation of Divine kingship over all the earth's inhabitants.
